pull.body:
Group: R11-PRE-ROUND-CHECK-GATE (topic r11-pre-round-check-gate)
Cards: E11-N-NULL-REVIEWER (accepted by tvofi, "Accept both (Recommended)"); tvofi's 2026-11-15 ruling "Only the finder critical are required for finder start", with his 14:00Z correction that what is still open when the finders finish goes to the architect and planner.
Code-owned and policy: tools/audit/check_scopes.py, dev/governance/decisions/0018-objective-function.md (sections 5 and 6) and dev/governance/roles/architect-planner.md need tvofi's approving review, or one under mandate 6893738184 (issue 3394, scope all, to 2026-12-15T12:00Z).

`check_scopes.py --round N` refused round 11's start on every accepted evaluation card not yet merged, the finder-critical ones and the rest alike: 43 lines at the evaluation's approved head. The owner ruled only the finder-critical ones gate the start. This change makes that ruling a structured field and has the check read it:

- **`gates_finders`**, a boolean on each accepted card, written by the orchestrator beside `ruling`. 0018 section 5 already lets the orchestrator write the owner's ruling into a card; the field records what that ruling decided about finder gating, so it is part of the ruling. The evaluator's `finder_critical` prose stays as the evaluator's argument. It is not parsed, because four cards (E11-K-D4, D5, D9, D10) read "no as the card stands" while the owner's ruling on them is "All four before finders", so the prose does not decide. The check refuses an accepted card whose `gates_finders` is missing or not a boolean ("yes", 1 and null are all refused), so no card stops gating by accident. A rejected or deferred card needs no value.
- **At the finder start**, an accepted card with `gates_finders: false` that is not merged is not a gap. It is printed `PARALLEL <card> accepted, not merged, gates no finder: ...` because it is built while the finders run. Its unset `threshold`/`criterion` is not a gap either: it is built with the card. A non-gating card that is merged gets every check an accepted card gets (after the review, changes its file). A gating card is checked as before.
- **For P3**, `--round N --open-cards` prints `{round, open_cards, unmarked_cards, ref}` as JSON and exits, rc 1 with an `UNMARKED <card>` line on stderr for each accepted card with no boolean `gates_finders` (see `### Repair`). Run at the ref where P3 starts, it lists the non-gating accepted cards still unmerged then. It skips the scope verdict, so it is quick, and it exits 2 rather than printing an empty list when the evaluation is not tracked at the ref. Why a flag rather than parsing the PARALLEL lines: P3 runs at a different moment from the finder start, and the architect needs a parseable list without the 2-minute scope run.
- **The null reviewer** (E11-N-NULL-REVIEWER): `norm(ev.get("reviewer", ""))` turned JSON null into `none`, which is non-empty and so passed the two-seats rule. The evaluator and the reviewer must now each be a non-blank string before they are normalised. A null, absent, blank, `0` or `[]` value is refused for either seat.

Carry 0: this group's part-2 carry (body item 4ffa4b06, landed on the roster). It is built in part 2's own pull request (topic r11-pre-round-check-gate-p2), as the orchestrator ruled, not in this one.

## Approval

Not yet given. These policy edits are kept minimal and await tvofi's approving review at the head, or an approving review under mandate 6893738184 (issue 3394, scope all, to 2026-12-15T12:00Z), declared with the mandate id:
- 0018 section 5: the orchestrator's ruling field now includes `gates_finders` on an accepted card.
- 0018 section 6: Writes and Refuses name the field and the PARALLEL / `--open-cards` behaviour.
- architect-planner.md: Inputs now name `check_scopes.py --round <N> --open-cards` at P3's start. Step 3 places every open card in the plan once, like a finding. Paid within its token cap by dropping two duplicated phrases: "read-only on code", which "You do not write production code" already says, and the Method's "(sensitivity, tradeoff points)", which step 2 already says. The target's holdout bullet now points at step 7's list instead of repeating it.
- evaluator.md is unchanged: "never ... write a `ruling`" already covers a field that 0018 defines as part of the ruling.

## Head

`86a88d394c61d615dcc0107a6189e45ca7b4d219` merges the authored code head `8ad98806e4c824491455b50f05f16eaa09ac7ac9`.

8ad98806e4c824491455b50f05f16eaa09ac7ac9 (handoff/r11-pre-round-check-gate), the merge of the PR branch origin/fix/r11-pre-round-check-gate (691aa86b1e, the relay's tree-neutral merges of 07f969bf3d and fc369d59) into 89f08b6d46; its tree is 89f08b6d46's, byte for byte (`git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` equal before and after the merge), so every figure taken at 89f08b6d46 describes it. 89f08b6d46 is one commit on 07f969bf3d (the round-2 repair of fix review 3620): the grader stubs part 2 needs, moved here by the orchestrator's route (a) for part 2's bootstrap question. The diff since 07f969bf3d is `tools/policy/check-wave-script.mjs` only, test code, so every figure under the two `### Repair` sections still describes this head: none of them reads that file.

### Delta: the P3 grader stubs for part 2 (#3633)

- **Why**: part 2 (#3633, ec058220b5) restores `audit-plan.js`'s refusal of a plan that leaves an open card or group in no group. main's `check-wave-script.mjs` drives `audit-plan.js` with `plan/read` and `plan/moves` stubs that carry no `--open-cards` listing, so it cannot grade that `audit-plan.js`: `ci_predict.py` reads that as a bootstrap (the base's grader refuses the head's workflow).
- **What moved**: exactly the stub hunks of `git diff origin/main ec058220b5 -- tools/policy/check-wave-script.mjs` (8 added, 4 removed lines): the `OPEN` listing (`open`: one open card E11-X, one open group R11-G, none unmarked; `open_rc` 0) spread into the default `plan/read` stub and the two triage `pthrows` reads; and `MOVES()`, the default `plan/moves` stub, which accounts for both items (E11-X in group A's `open_items`, R11-G in `dropped` with a reason). The refusal's own tests (the five new `pthrows`, the kept-group null control, the `--open-cards` read-prompt assertion) stay in part 2: they fail against an `audit-plan.js` without the refusal. Compared line for line: the delta's `+`/`-` lines are a subset of that diff's, and the remainder is exactly those seven tests.
- **Failing first** (the null control): main's grader, unchanged, against ec058220b5's `audit-plan.js` failed 7: the six `pthrows` named `a triage that drops a verified finding stops P3`, `a triage that keeps one finding twice stops P3`, `a group with no move entry stops P3`, `a publish that is not a 40-hex commit stops P3`, `a reviewer answering for another tree stops P3`, `a recorded verdict that is not a 40-hex commit stops P3`, and `the P3 plan workflow threw`, each with `check_scopes.py --open-cards exited undefined, not 0`.
- **Mutation**: the delta adds no `.py` line, so prepr's step 6d draws no mutant from it. The mutant that matters is the delta's removal, which is the null control above: 7 failures.

### Repair (fix review 3620, round 2)

- **Block**: main()'s `sys.exit(rc)` and its `print(line, file=sys.stderr)` were reached by no arm; M17 (exit 0) and M18 (no UNMARKED line) survived the full self-test.
- **Fix** (the reviewer's first option, at the command line): `open_cards_cli()` builds a scratch git repository in a temp directory with `tests/throwaway_git.py`'s `throwaway_git_init` (7248e2b3's raw `git init` was refused by prepr.sh's throwaway-git step; 07f969bf runs the repository and the subprocess under its environment) with two commits of a round-8 record (minimal objective and round-7 record) and runs `check_scopes.py --repo <tmp> --ref <commit> --round 8 --open-cards` as a subprocess on each. The two records differ only in `gates_finders` on C2 and C3: booleans in the first; absent on C2 and the string `"true"` on C3 in the second. C1 is accepted, `gates_finders: false`, unmerged; C4 is rejected.
- **Arms** (two, in `--self-test`'s coverage table):
  - null control: the all-boolean record exits 0, its stderr carries no `UNMARKED`, and its JSON `open_cards` is `["C1"]`;
  - the unmarked record exits 1, the stderr `UNMARKED` lines are exactly `UNMARKED C2`, `UNMARKED C3` (text before the colon, in order), and its JSON `unmarked_cards` is `["C2", "C3"]`.
- Rejected: moving main()'s print-and-exit into a function the self-test calls; the brief requires the CLI run as a subprocess, and a function arm would leave the `sys.exit` line itself unpinned.

### Repair (fix review 3620, round 1)

- **Block**: `--open-cards` printed `open_cards: []` and exited 0 on a record whose accepted cards carry no `gates_finders`, and nothing tested its output (M11 survived).
- **Fix**: `open_cards_report(rnd, tree, show, merged, anc, changed)` is the function main() prints. It lists the open non-gating cards and names each accepted card with no boolean `gates_finders`. It prints `UNMARKED <card>: accepted, no boolean gates_finders ...` to stderr, adds `unmarked_cards` to the JSON, and exits 1. The no-evaluation path still exits 2.
- **Tests**: the self-test drives `open_cards_report` through the same synthetic record as the other evaluation arms.
  - A non-gating unmerged card is listed: `({"round": 8, "open_cards": ["C1"], "unmarked_cards": []}, 0, [])`.
  - A complete record lists nothing, rc 0 (null control).
  - An accepted card with no `gates_finders`, or with `"no"`, is named, rc 1, whether merged or not.
  - The evaluation arms now hold 62 of 62.
- **Mutants**: `mutant_run.py --spec <scratch mutants3.json> --in-place --cmd "python3 <scratch evtest.py>"`. NULL survived and 4 of 4 were killed:
  - M11: `out` is dropped from the `evaluation_gaps` call, the reviewer's mutant.
  - M12: rc is always 0.
  - M13: no card is ever unmarked.
  - M14: only a missing value counts as unmarked, so `"no"` passes.
- **Live**: `python3 tools/audit/check_scopes.py --repo . --ref f6d35cf73f19a053c99e6627071984ff4190aa04 --round 11 --open-cards` exits 1 with `"open_cards": []` and 43 `unmarked_cards`, and prints 43 UNMARKED lines on stderr. The null control is the same evaluation with every card marked (above): no card is unmarked.
- **After the owner's values landed** (eval/r11 c6ce415b77, `gates_finders` written by the orchestrator from the rulings): the same command exits 0 with no UNMARKED line, `unmarked_cards: []`, and 12 `open_cards`. Those 12 are exactly the cards whose value is false: E11-GATE-REDS, E11-INJECTED, E11-N-GATE-CAUSE, E11-N-INSTRUMENT-YIELD, E11-N-INTAKE-BUILDER, E11-N-NULL-REVIEWER, E11-N-ROLE-CLAUSE, E11-N-RULE-YIELD, E11-R-WORKFLOWS, E11-S-SEATS, E11-SCORECARD and E11-T-product_green_floor.

## Mutation proof

### Round 2 (fix review 3620, at 07f969bf3d)

The reviewer's driver (`verdict/3620:evidence/mut_driver.py`), with M20 and M21 added and M11, M13-M15 (judged in round 1) dropped: each mutant is applied to `tools/audit/check_scopes.py` in place, `python3 tools/audit/check_scopes.py --repo . --ref HEAD --self-test` is run whole, and a mutant is KILLED on a non-zero rc. The file was compared byte for byte with its copy afterwards (`cmp`, printed RESTORED).
- NULL: rc 0, SURVIVED, `marked rc=0, unmarked rc=1 ['UNMARKED C2', 'UNMARKED C3']`.
- M17 main's `sys.exit(rc)` -> `sys.exit(0)`: KILLED (the CLI's unmarked rc reads 0).
- M18 main's `print(line, file=sys.stderr)` -> `pass`: KILLED (no UNMARKED line).
- M20 that print -> `print(line)` (to stdout): KILLED (no UNMARKED line on stderr, stdout no longer JSON).
- M21 main's `sys.exit(rc)` -> `sys.exit(1)`: KILLED by the null control alone (marked rc reads 1).
- M12 and M16 (round 1's function mutants): KILLED, now by the CLI arms as well.
- M19 `"open_cards": sorted(out)` -> unsorted: SURVIVED, an equivalent mutant: `evaluation_gaps` appends to `parallel` while iterating `sorted(cards.items())`, so `out` is already sorted and the `sorted()` is a no-op on every input. No arm can kill it; the reviewer's follow-up is disposed here rather than carried.

Failing test first. The new self-test arms ran against the unchanged predicates, with only the parameter added: `evaluation_self_test` held 54 of 59. These five failed:
- a non-gating accepted card not merged passes and is listed beside
- a non-gating unmerged card's unset value is no gap, it builds with the card
- an accepted card with no boolean gates_finders is refused, in every shape
- an accepted card with no gates_finders is refused even unmerged, and never listed beside

At the head all 59 hold.

There is one mutant per new predicate, run with `python3 tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --spec <scratch mutants.json> --in-place --cmd "python3 <scratch evtest.py>"`. The driver calls `check_scopes.evaluation_self_test` at HEAD and exits 1 on any failing arm. NULL survived, and every mutant was killed:
- M1 `if not isinstance(gating, bool)` -> `if False`
- M2 -> `if gating is None` (accepts "yes")
- M3 `elif not gating and not (c and merged(c))` -> `elif not gating`

- M6 the `continue` after it deleted
- M7 the old `norm(ev.get(k, ""))`

## Null control

The evaluation at origin/eval-review/r11-4 (f6d35cf73f) was run through `evaluation_gaps` at that ref, using a scratch driver that substitutes the card fields:
- **As written** (no `gates_finders`): 92 gaps. These are the 49 of today plus 43 "carries no boolean gates_finders", so an unrecorded card refuses and never passes silently.

This is line for line identical to `check_scopes.py --repo . --ref origin/eval-review/r11-4 --round 11` on main's code (compared as lists in the driver, printing "identical" only on equality), and 0 PARALLEL.
- **The proposed gating list** (31 true, 12 false; held outside this PR for the orchestrator to record): 36 gaps (31 not merged), 12 PARALLEL.

## Figures

- Delta, the grader matrix. Command: `node tools/policy/check-wave-script.mjs` from the tree root, with `.claude/workflows/audit-plan.js` replaced by `git show <rev>:.claude/workflows/audit-plan.js` and restored after (`git checkout`); the result line is the script's `N passed, M failed` and its rc. Every run also prints `FAIL (probe, expected) threw: deliberate`, the script's own block-harness probe, counted in neither number.
  - main 6aa7ddc712 grader, unchanged, x ec058220b5 `audit-plan.js`: `209 passed, 7 failed`, rc 1 (the null control).
  - main grader unchanged x 416280f5 `audit-plan.js` (blob 0a06aa738b, the same as main's and this head's): `223 passed, 0 failed`, rc 0.
  - main grader plus these stubs x ec058220b5: `223 passed, 0 failed`, rc 0; x 416280f5: `223 passed, 0 failed`, rc 0.
  - this head's grader x ec058220b5: `223 passed, 0 failed`, rc 0; x 416280f5: `223 passed, 0 failed`, rc 0.
  - The brief's 230/230 is part 2's grader: ec058220b5's `check-wave-script.mjs` x ec058220b5's `audit-plan.js`, on main's tree, printed `230 passed, 0 failed`. With the stubs alone the count is 223 at both revisions; the seven tests left in part 2 are the difference.
- Round 2, at 07f969bf3d: `python3 tools/audit/check_scopes.py --repo . --ref HEAD --self-test` printed `evaluation arms: 62/62 held; --round 1 rc=1; --open-cards rc=2, marked rc=0, unmarked rc=1 ['UNMARKED C2', 'UNMARKED C3']` and `SELF-TEST passed (every perturbed scope refused)`.

R11-PRE-MACHINERY-LIMITER, part 1 of 3: card P2 (owner ruling 2026-11-13) and the group's carries 0-4. Carry 5, Carry 6, Carry 7, Carry 8, Carry 9, Carry 10, Carry 11 and Carry 12 are parts 2 and 3, dispatched at this handoff. Carry 13 (P793, the closure runbook scripts' orch-root default) was homed on the group by tvofi 2026-11-15 after this part's dispatch, so it is in neither this part's brief nor this repair round's (body only); this pull request does not build it, and which part builds it is the orchestrator's assignment.

**P2, the target.** `machinery_ratchet.py` gains THE TARGET (its docstring is the rule): `dev/governance/config/machinery_target_budgets.json` holds `anchor`, `every_merges` and `step`, and the target is `nonproduction_merges - step * floor(n / every_merges)`, n the first-parent merges after the anchor up to the base (PR mode) or head (push mode), never below 0, compared against target plus the existing band. **The schedule:** anchor `b3831ff64e` (this branch's merge base, where the cap was recorded), 48 down every 290 merges: 290 is half the frozen `window_merges` (the owner's seven days of merges), 48 is 10% of the recorded 478 rounded half up (the audit's "e.g. -10% per week", section 6 row a2). **The enumerator:** `python3 tools/audit/machinery_ratchet.py --measure --head origin/main` now prints `target` and `merges_past_anchor`; `--check` prints a `target` line. At a round start the orchestrator records the cap down to `--measure` and asks the owner for the round's anchor and step (`ratchet-budgets.md`); `budget_raise_gate.py` classifies a moved anchor, a longer `every_merges` or a smaller `step` as a raise.

Why a second budgets file and not three keys in `machinery_budgets.json`: `governance.yml` grades a pull request with the BASE's `machinery_ratchet.py`, whose `load_budgets` refuses a key it does not read, so the keys there would turn `policy-docs` red on this pull request (a BOOTSTRAP split, `fixer.md` step 5). The new file is invisible to the base copy, and it is a `*_budgets.json`, so the raise gate guards it; a constant in the program would not be guarded (the program is not code-owned).

Where it binds, a design choice: only a non-production, unexempted candidate in PR mode. A production candidate cannot raise the metric, and the existing code refuses any candidate when the window is over the cap, so a binding target under the old semantics would refuse production work. In push mode the target is a report line: a schedule overtaking the window would otherwise turn a required check on main red with nothing to repair. The two caps stay the ceiling in both modes. **For the owner's review:** a machinery repair of a red required check on main is refused by the target like any machinery merge once the window is past it; its routes are the band, an earned exemption, or an owner-approved change to the schedule. The alternative, a ground the offline ratchet would have to read, was not taken.

**P2, the rest.** `proposal-triage.md`: on severity only a red required check on main or a blocked production pull request skips the machinery bars (`medium`, `high`, `major`, `critical` no longer do); root-cause countermeasure, closeout and owner directive keep their routes, which are not severity. `ratchet-budgets.md`: one in, one out for required checks, the set `merge_train.py owed-reds` prints.

**Carry 0, Carry 1 and Carry 2, the instrument freeze** (`orchestrator.md`, replacing the "proposal waits" bullet; Carry 1's owner and outside items also in the scope bullet and the playbook's round start): local prototype under `$HPO_STATE_DIR/r<N>/proto/<id>/`, each use a sweep-log `WORKAROUND <id> onset=<UTC> cost=<min>` line; the permanent fix a numbered entry of the proposals file in `$HPO_STATE_DIR/r<N>/` citing the prototype and its measured effect; consolidated (duplicates merged, uses and cost summed) and triaged once at round end; ACCEPTs built at the next round's start before its finders, the rest refused with their numbers; a workaround never changes production code, loosens a gate or budget, or skips a review; the exceptions are a production defect, an owner order, a red required check on main, and an owner or outside item. The scope bullet now folds an undeferred owner or outside item into the ongoing round. The playbook's round start gains step 4 (where the prior round's proposals and prototypes are, and that its ACCEPTs are built before finders); step 5 (was 4) already states the deferral record (who, when, their words) and that silence is none.

**Carry 3:** `nonproduction_merges` re-recorded 521 -> 478 (more than its band of 5 below the cap); `churn_per_kilo_product_lines` stays (13785 against 14797, inside its band of 3636). **Carry 4:** `pr_cap.py` classes open pull requests by `machinery_ratchet.is_product` (one predicate), `dispatch-gate --machinery OWNER/REPO` refuses a machinery group once machinery and unread pull requests fill the slots production does not hold (`replan.py` `DEFAULT_CAPS` slots less `PRODUCTION_SLOTS`), and `orchestrator_tick.py`'s cap levels print `pr_cap.class_line` every pass (five lines there; the batch's L5 hold on that instrument covers proposals, and P742 routes this carry here).

Payment for the policy caps: `ratchet-budgets.md` lost three spent sentences (two historical measurements of the CLAUDE.md split and the "deferred, not disabled" motivation); `dev/audit/README.md` lost the organization-transfer item, ruled out by tvofi 2026-11-14 (`dev/programme/HANDOVER.md`, the designer's answers), cut to one line.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant applied alone at the head, its self-test run, the file restored:

## Null control

- `target: no file, no target: the refused candidate passes (null control)`: the same machinery candidate at the same base passes once the target file is gone.
- `target: 1 merge past the anchor is still 2, so a machinery candidate at 2 passes`: the schedule, not the window, refuses.
- `null controls: an empty board passes it, and no --machinery never reads the board`: the same `main()` call with an empty board exits 0, and without `--machinery` prints no machinery line.
- `target: the band is added to it, at the boundary`: band 1 refuses the candidate band 2 passes, so the pass is the band's.
- `null control: one free machinery slot passes`; `null control: below the machinery slots the line is not flagged`; `target: null control` (an unchanged target file is no raise).

pull.body:
R11-PRE-RELAY-REBUILD part 1 of 3 (owner card P12, 2026-11-13): roster carries 0-4. Carries 5-12 are later parts, dispatched at this handoff, and none is answered here.

- **Carry 0 (#3358's silent skip).** The skip came from the handoff arm's topic. `cloud_relay.sh` turned `fix/<t>-pr` into `<t>` alone (`topic_grammar.pr_topic`). `review_packet.py`'s handoff-not-applied read tries `<t>-pr` first and then `<t>`. #3358's repair returned under `handoff/r10-combi-tank-pr`, so the arm read only `handoff/r10-combi-tank`. That ref held an older tip, already in the head, whose body the relay had applied (its last update of #3358 ended OK on 2026-11-09). So the arm took the `continue` for "ancestor, body applied", with no line, while `bus.sh dispatch` refused handoff-not-applied. The rule now has one owner, `topic_grammar.handoff_topics`, moved out of `review_packet.py` and used by both readers through `topic_grammar.py handoff-topics`. The first topic that has a `handoff/` ref decides. `handoff_level`'s open and merged topic lists use the same rule, so `handoff/<t>-pr` with an open PR is no longer `handoff-no-pr`. Every other skip of a handoff that the head lacks is now owed on `<log>.level`. A missing body is `handoff-held ... NOBODY`, mirroring HELD-BODY. A hold-file skip is `handoff-held ... HOLD`. An unreadable ref or head, a busy tools tree, a BUSY update and an unreadable body are each `handoff-skipped <ref> <tip> #<pr> <why>`. These kinds are rewritten every pass.
- **Carry 1 (S14-TICK-STALE-SILENT).** `tick_loop.sh`'s `fresh_check` now restarts a branch-backed checkout that is clean and holds no commit outside origin/main (`checkout -q -B <branch> origin/main`). A branch that has commits of its own stays stale, with the why `the branch <b> holds <n> commit(s) origin/main lacks; it is never moved`. When a stale state lasts into a second consecutive pass (counted in `<out>.stale`), the board ends with `-> OWED relay-skipped code=<sha7> behind=<n>: <why> (stale <k> consecutive passes)`.
- **Carry 2 (S14-RELAY-CADENCE).** In the sleep between passes, `relay_gap_sleep` reaps a finished relay and starts the next one under the same lock once `HPO_TICK_RELAY_GAP` seconds (default 120, digits only) have passed since that relay ended. The holder now writes the end epoch as a third field of `<out>.relay.rc`. The tick keeps `--interval`. A stale pass starts no relay in its sleep, and neither does a relay that is still in flight.
- **Carry 3 (HELD-REVIEW over a returned verdict).** `review_freeze` now asks whether the dispatch's own `probe/rev-<pr>-<nonce8>` exists and is in `cloud-relayed.refused` or disposed in the ledger. If so, the review is over: the arm prints `RELEASED-REVIEW` and runs the update. Otherwise the HELD-REVIEW line and its level line name the probe's state: `probe=none (in flight)`, `probe=<sha8> relayed, not yet on verdict/<pr>`, or `probe=<sha8> held by the relay (dispose it to release)`.
- **Carry 4 (owed red text to a cloud seat).** Take a `handoff-wip/<topic>` BLOCKED.md that names `body_push: REFUSED PREDICTOR` and whose `PREDICT <check>` lines name a check in `merge_train.py owed-reds`. For it, the carry-fold arm reads that check at the topic's open PR head (`failure_logs.sh`: name, conclusion, error lines) into `<state>/cloud-owed-red-<topic>.md`, and the `carry-fold` level line names that file for the seat's next message. The carry-fold memo keeps the judged line, so the check is read once for each (wip, body) pair.

Alternatives not taken, and why each lost:
- Carry 0: stripping `-pr` in the relay and adding `<t>-pr` as a second read beside it. That would keep two copies of the rule that diverged once already.
- Carry 0: "any candidate not an ancestor decides". The relay would then disagree with `review_packet.py`'s first-with-a-ref rule.
- Carry 3: a timer release. It would release a review that is genuinely in flight.

pull.title: R11-OUTSIDE-APPLY-PLAN-CEILING: apply plan only up to the manual-plan window
pull.body:
Closes #3636

"Apply this plan" failed whenever the published plan had a run starting 20 hours or more from now. The card's `apply()` trimmed the draft at the edit floor only, so it sent runs past the manual-plan window that the editor itself would not let the user touch, and `build_override` in `manual_plan.py` refuses any slot starting past now plus the window. The card now drops every run starting at or after `ceilingParts().applyEnd` (now plus the published `manual_plan_window_hours`) less `APPLY_CLOCK_SKEW_MS`. It does not use `editCeiling`, which also takes the zoomed visible end into account, so a zoomed-in view does not change what is applied. The lower bound is unchanged. A run straddling the window is still sent whole, because the backend frees every step past the expiry itself. The backend refusal is untouched: it protects the stored plan across restarts.

Clock skew: the card measures the window from the browser's clock and the service measures it from the server's. `APPLY_CLOCK_SKEW_MS` is one plan step (`PLAN_STEP_MS`). Runs start on step boundaries, so holding back a run that starts in the last step before the ceiling costs at most one step of pinned time before the expiry, and a browser clock up to one step fast is still accepted. If the browser clock is slow, the card only drops runs the server would also have accepted, so nothing is sent that the server refuses. Alternatives considered: (a) relaxing the backend refusal, which the brief rules out because a slot starting past the window corrupts the stored plan at the next restart; (b) clamping a run's start to the ceiling instead of dropping it, which would invent a slot the plan never had; (c) no skew allowance, which leaves the reported failure reachable on any browser clock that runs fast (mutant M2 below).

No user-facing text changes. Release note for the stamper: credit the reporter, GitHub user rasenschachmatt, for the report and the suggested fix.

## Head

`c57638046f9d2477d761e8da56327369f8a9a4fe` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

1dba0f90a234562412e127e1aa53c1476b2ba49f, measured against origin/main 47f0f18a7ecebaa0f6ff0e4948b4f8d82e616e1a (merge base e30408f7881cd5602a2c4d7ea9517b0d765652f6) at 2026-11-16T01:48Z. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0, so main is not merged in.

Review round 2: the delta since the reviewed head 87a315a355faa219065ed906ed3adbd4d589aacd is one commit that touches only `tests/card.mjs`; no production change. It adds two checks to the #3636 block. `a zoomed-in view does not change the applied runs (#3636)` zooms the view so the visible end is 3 h before the window (`geomAt` returns `windowEnd` 3 h before the ceiling). It requires `editCeiling()` to be at or before that point and the dhw payload to stay `[[-4,-3],[-2,0.5]]`. `a run starting two steps before the window is sent (#3636)` seeds a space run `[-0.5, 1]` h from the ceiling and requires it to be sent. The first check pins the design choice that the ceiling is `applyEnd` and not `editCeiling()`; the second pins that the skew allowance is no wider than one step. The block's `extended()` and `applied()` helpers gained an optional seeded-run set and an optional geometry so the two checks reuse them.

## Mutation proof

Run in a detached worktree at the head, `HPO_PLANDATA` pointed at the payload `tests/plan_view.py` wrote, then `node tests/card.mjs`:

pull.title: R11-OUTSIDE-SLAB-SEED-GUARD: r11 outside slab seed guard
pull.body:
Refs #3616: the planning defect its diagnostics showed, not the issue's multi-zone request, which stays open for the room-level steps the owner's reply lists. No `Closes`.

A floor-return reading seeded the slab estimate every cycle (`ThermalModel.update_slab_from_return_temp`, merged 0.7 sensor / 0.3 model) behind only the `FLOOR_WATER_RANGE_C` range check. A heat-pump return on a buffer plant in that field reads far above any floor loop, so the slab estimate believes heat is stored and the plan holds none. New pure module `slab_seed.py` owns the decision:

- **Bound** `SLAB_SEED_MAX_ABOVE_ROOM_K = 12.0` (argued in its comment): floor-loop water runs 3-9 K above room air (the band the `lower_floor_modelled` repair already states); EN 1264's surface limits (29 C occupied, 33 C bathroom, over 20 / 24 C design rooms) put the floor 9 K above its room; 3 K margin for a manifold sensor and a peripheral zone. A reading more than 12 K above the room is refused.
- **Model estimate**: a refused reading leaves the slab to the model's own estimate, by the exact path an install with no floor-return sensor takes (`_async_learn_interval(slab_unsensed=True)`, then `_propagated_slab` or the room+1 K first seed). Measured identical below (refused arm == unconfigured arm, slab trajectory and plan).
- **Hot-water runs and defrost**: a reading is refused while the pump's observed mode is hot water alone (`slab_seed.hot_water_run`: `mode_observed`, `dhw`, not `space_heat`) or a defrost is flagged (asked of the `defrost_standoff` owner, `freq_control.defrost_interval`, per `tests/entities.py`'s P2 registry).
- **Repair** `floor_return_implausible`, a `ConfigNotices` warning naming the sensor, its reading, the room and the bound; raised on the level alone (a hot-water or defrost refusal is the plant working, not a wrong sensor) and cleared on the next plausible cycle. No stored option is migrated.
- **Texts**: the floor-return option description (config and both options pages, en/de/sv) says which sensor belongs there and states the bound; README's sensor table says the Optimal Setpoint is the step's planned power scaled onto the coldest..warmest acceptable range (`HeatPumpOptimizer._power_to_setpoints`), not a target temperature, and its repair list gives the new repair a home.

Timing (decision): the coordinator seeds the published state before this cycle's pump signals are read, so the first call (`slab_seed.seed`) judges on last cycle's signals, and `slab_seed.judge`, after the signals are read, re-decides on this cycle's before the slab is finalised. Alternatives that lost: moving the pump-signal read above the floor-return read reorders the reader's health snapshot and every learner between; seeding only after the signals are read moves what the learners between see, so plausible installs would not stay byte-identical.

The bound is one-sided: a reading below the room is not refused. That direction plans more heat, not none, and no report shows it; out of this fix's scope.

## Head

`74a57885a3ef178f2556b4b105063a2b3a2edd9a` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`74a57885a3ef178f2556b4b105063a2b3a2edd9a` is this PR's head: `59070bb608` (the delivery row) plus the `mutation-autofix` commit `74a57885a3` (`ci: pin killed mutants`, ledger files under `tests/mutation_ledger/` only, no production line). The code below is unchanged from the measured tree; this body re-renders the figure block at this head against the PR's recorded base `5825e1346c14eecace5c87c046558774145a94dc` (origin/main at the re-render is 6aa7ddc712, which `git merge-tree --write-tree` merges with this head without a conflict; 2026-11-16T02:05Z).

a902e7fad4046ecbbcb115186ef4fdd5cc770aed, measured against merge base cb19070965d76b84d9a221d4dfb05c7c9b8efbf7, origin/main's tip (committed 2026-11-15T22:29:46+01:00) at 2026-11-15T22:15Z. The branch was cut at 66865be375 and merged origin/main cb19070965 (conflicts in the package counts, resolved in the merge commit's message); the evidence below is re-taken at that head unless it names another tree.

## Mutation proof

Block: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/seat/features_block.py --prelude "exec(open('<prelude>').read())" '# --- #3616: an implausible slab seed'`, prelude from `features_block.py --emit-prelude <prelude> '# --- #3616: an implausible slab seed'`. Unmutated: `ALL 9 FEATURES BLOCK PASSED`.

- Failing first (the coordinator, strings and translations at the merge base, `slab_seed.py` present but unwired): `6 of 9 FEATURES BLOCK FAILED`: `#3616: a 38 C heat-pump return ... no longer plans zero space heating` (`planned 0.000 kWh, slab [37.47, 38.54, 38.86, 38.96, 38.99, 39.0]`), `and a refused reading leaves the slab to the model exactly as an install with no floor-return sensor does`, `and a repair issue names the sensor and the bound`, `a hot-water-only run does not seed the slab from the return`, `nor does a defrost`, `every floor-return option text names the bound the guard applies`. The null control and the two predicate checks passed.
- Bound removed (`above_room` returns `False`): `4 of 9 FAILED`, the zero-plan, model-equivalence, repair and bound checks.
- Early gate removed (the first call seeds unconditionally): `3 of 9 FAILED`, model-equivalence, hot-water and defrost.
- Defrost arm off: `1 of 9 FAILED`, `nor does a defrost`. Hot-water arm off: `1 of 9 FAILED`, `a hot-water-only run does not seed the slab from the return`.
- Diff drive: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --diff 66865be375...HEAD --path custom_components --max-mutants 80 --report-only --cmd '<the block command>'` at ac80188f36 (slab_seed.py and coordinator.py as at the head) drafts 27 mutants (`--list` counts them) and prints one line, `SURVIVED custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/slab_seed.py:59 RETURN_DEL`, rc 0: an equivalent mutant (`refusal`'s trailing `return None`), triaged in `tests/mutation_ledger/survivor_triage/slab_seed.py/refusal.RETURN_DEL.da9e8e97.json`.

Head: `12.689 kWh`, slab equal to the unconfigured install's.
- Bound edge: `slab_seed.above_room(32.0, 20.0)` False, `(32.1, 20.0)` True (the block's bound check; the `>=` mutant is killed there).
- Seams of the class, by `awk '/async def _update_current_state/,/def _refresh_model_corrections/' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py | grep -oE "reader\.read[a-z_]*\(CONF_[A-Z_]+" | sort | uniq -c`: 13 reads. The class is a reading that seeds a model state for a different physical quantity than it measures. `FLOOR_RETURN_TEMP` (water, seeding the slab): closed here. `INDOOR_TEMP`, `LOWER_FLOOR_TEMP`, `OUTDOOR_TEMP`, `DHW_TEMP`, `BUFFER_TANK_TEMP`, `WOOD_TANK_TOP`, `WOOD_TANK_BOTTOM`: each seeds the quantity it measures, outside the class. `MIXING_VALVE_TARGET` (a set-point read as a room temperature): already guarded by the `valve_target_above_comfort` repair. `SOLAR_RADIATION`, `ENERGY`, `POWER`, `HOUSE_POWER`: not temperatures, seed no thermal state.
- Structure: `python3 tests/structure.py` passes every row at the head; the first draft breached `class_excess_loc` +9, `max_class_loc` +9 and `max_cc` +1, paid by moving the decision into `slab_seed` (`seed`, `judge`) and correcting the coordinator's last-resort comment, which predated refused readings.
- Typing: `python3 tests/typing_ruler.py` `ALL 9 ... PASSED`, `ALL 12 ... PASSED` (a first draft added one `arg-type`: `seed` now takes `float | None`).
- Scoped gate: `GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=cb19070965 ./tests/run.sh` at 12fc864c4a (the merge): `MODE: SCOPED -- 23 script(s) run`, 22 ok, `tests/entities.py` red on one check, `the lane's docstring records those measured numbers as the selection-cost note` (`163 of the 528` pairs now, 162 written), corrected at the head; `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` at the head `ALL 2723 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`. `tests/features.py` whole script ok in that run (714 s), the #3616 block included. `tests/doc_claims.py` `ALL 410 checks PASSED`. `tests/harness_headers.py` passes with the round-4 D6 header and output re-recorded for 94 modules (main's `running_signal.py` and this branch's `slab_seed.py`).

- Architecture score: `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff cb19070965` prints `Architecture score: dS -0.0006 WORSENS (inadmissible: coord_footprint 2495->2496)` at the head against cb19070965 as against 66865be375, answered under `## Architecture score`.

Folding the call into the `_async_learn_interval` argument with a walrus would read flat and only hide the statement.

pull.title: R11-PRE-PLAN-RENDER: r11 pre plan render
pull.body:
R11-PRE-PLAN-RENDER (part 1): the plan page shows every phase of the round.
Group R11-PRE-PLAN-RENDER, roster lane IN, size M; owner directive (tvofi, 2026-11-15): "Make the plan html show all phases in the round".
The round's phases are drawn from a tracked, linted per-round file, never from round-specific code.

Until now the plan page drew roster groups only. Between a round's start and its fix roster, it showed nothing of the round. This change adds `tools/audit/seat/plan_phases.py`, which owns the phases file, its refusals and its section. `plan_page.py` draws that section above the group lanes. Round 11's own file, `dev/programme/round11/phases.json`, holds the round's state as of 2026-11-15 13:00Z.

- The file is `dev/programme/round<N>/phases.json`: the round, `as_of`, and one entry per playbook phase (`dev/audit/README.md`, "Running a round: the playbook" and "Round start"). The phases, in the playbook's order, are round start, finders, verify and judge, the architect plan, fix waves, stamps and closure. Each entry carries a status (not started, running, waiting on a named thing, done), started and finished dates, an optional forecast window with its basis, entry and exit text, and items.
- The schema refuses: an unknown status or phase; a phase out of the playbook's order or repeated; `waiting` with nothing named; a date that is not ISO-8601 UTC; a started or finished date on a not-started phase; a finished date on a phase not done; and a forecast with no basis. `plan_phases.py --check FILE` exits 1 on any of them.
- The page draws a phase the file does not list as "not started", never omits it. A date the file does not carry is a dash. The page prints no date or count the file does not carry. Items are drawn under every phase not done.
- One page: the phases section plus everything `plan_page.py` drew before, unchanged (owner, 2026-11-15: "The generic plan page should support showing fixer groups as per normal in addition to the phases"). The phases are drawn on the swimlanes' own time axis (`plan_page.time_axis`, the one axis function both use). A phase reaching past either end is cut there and labelled, for example "since Sun 15 Nov 05:22"; a phase or forecast wholly off the axis is named in its row, not drawn. The section says that the fix waves are the group lanes below; the round-start items name their groups and do not repeat their lanes. The page renders in three cases: groups and phases; phases only (a roster with no fix group yet, as at a round's start); and groups only (no phases file, drawn exactly as before).
- `plan_page.py --phases FILE` draws the named file. Without it, the page draws the checkout's highest-numbered `dev/programme/round<N>/phases.json`. An invalid file draws its section as PHASES UNAVAILABLE and the rest of the page still renders. A checkout with no phases file draws no section, so the page is unchanged.
- The page names the file by its checkout-relative path, never a host path, so `plan_public.py`'s privacy refusal still passes on a page with phases.
- `plan_phases.py --phases FILE --html OUT` draws the section alone as a page in the plan page's stylesheet, for a round with no plan.json at all. The published page is `plan_page.py`'s, with both halves.

What the plan beat needs to pick the file up: nothing new. The beat's `plan-beat` row runs `state_docs.py --plan`, which runs `plan_page.py --repo <its checkout>`. Discovery reads `dev/programme/round*/phases.json` from that checkout's working tree, so the round-11 phases appear once the beat's checkout is at a main that holds this merge. Keeping the phases current is an edit to that file on main: the orchestrator's record step, like the roster.

Roster carries of R11-PRE-PLAN-RENDER, each named. Carry 0 (round filter), Carry 1 (next-round tab with its own preliminary Gantt), Carry 2 (the two-tab prototype as the model), Carry 3 (description, strip and lede counts), Carry 4 (PC-1113-05) and Carry 5 (plan-beat items P753 and P794) are the group's later parts, and this change leaves their text and scope as written. Today's behaviour is byte-identical with no phases file (measured below), the phases section is self-contained so a tab can host it unchanged, and no beat change is needed.

Carry 6 (the owner's directive to show every phase of the round) is built here, apart from two of its items that remain on the group for its next part. First, phase dates from the plan's duration model: this change takes dates only from the phases file, where a forecast must name its basis, and adds no constant and no duration. ## Class repair: a file `--check` accepts is a file the page draws

Defect (reviewer): `plan_phases.violations` left text fields untyped, so a phases file `--check` accepts crashed `plan_phases.section` (reached from `plan_page.render`, `plan_page.py:710`). The instance was `entry: 5`. Measured at the prior head, driving the old validator over every node of a full file with junk values: `entry`, `exit`, `detail`, `note`, `basis` and `waiting_on`/`name` as numbers or lists crashed `html.escape` (AttributeError), and a list, dict or `{}` as `status` or `phase` crashed `violations` itself (TypeError: unhashable), as did `items` not a list (not iterable).

Fix, one owner: `plan_phases.violations` types every text field the section prints (`_TEXT_DOC`, `_TEXT_PHASE`, `_TEXT_ITEM`; a forecast's `basis` and an item's `name` with their presence checks), `items` as a list and `status` as a string before it is a dictionary key. Alternative not taken: `str()` or `html.escape(str(x))` at the draw sites. It would turn a number into text silently and leave `violations` crashing on an unhashable status; refusing at the file is the one place the contract lives.

Enumeration rule (fixer.md step 8): the census `_census` in `plan_phases.fixture_checks` takes every node of a fully populated phases file (`_nodes`, not a list of field names) and replaces it with each of the ten junk values `_JUNK`; each result either earns a violation or draws in `section` (with the plan page's axis and without), and `violations` never raises. It asserts that the fixture populates every field the section reads, so a field the section starts reading has to be in the fixture. Every node the rule returns is closed: the count is asserted equal to `len(_JUNK) * (nodes - 1)` in the check "phases census: null control" (the number it ran is in its `got`, not carried here).

pull.body:
Records the owner's standing rulings in `dev/programme/RULINGS.md` and has the liveness hook re-read that file after a compaction when it changed. Roster group R11-PRE-RULINGS-FILE.

## Re-cut

Round 4. Owner rulings 2026-11-15 (tvofi): "The rulings file is not policy."; "Orchestrator.md at least should clearly refer to the rulings file. Rulings are binding, even if it is not policy." This body replaces the earlier ones; round history is dropped. What changed in this round: no file calls `RULINGS.md` policy; `orchestrator.md`, `fixer.md` and `proposal-triage.md` each carry one sentence that the owner's rulings in `dev/programme/RULINGS.md` bind though the file is not policy, and `CLAUDE.md`'s index line says the same; `RULINGS.md` stays in `dev/governance/config/corpus_excluded.json` and is in no policy list.

## Approval

Policy change (`CLAUDE.md`, `orchestrator.md`, `fixer.md`, `proposal-triage.md`), for tvofi's approving review at the head; it records the owner's 2026-11-15 rulings quoted in Re-cut. Approvable under mandate 6893738184 where the orchestrator holds it.

## Head

`f475901cacf05fc6b106610d90db01cff7e08a07` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`73fefc820a47594f2e95866f053c405d194b4a33`, on `origin/main` `31117b1029de63938d949e78dcbcd8f9451e5e33` (2026-11-15 UTC); `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reports no conflict, so main was not merged in.

## Hunks kept and dropped

Every hunk of the earlier diff in a contract, each judged by whether the rulings are relevant to that role (the owner's test):
- `orchestrator.md`, kept: one sentence before the compaction re-read stating the rulings bind the orchestrator and whoever it briefs and where they are; the compaction re-read of the file when changed; section 5's pointer to the soft cap's value in the file; the card-ruling edits (scoped prepr, `--allow-red`, local-seat rule, objective record), each a ruling the orchestrator carries out.
- `orchestrator.md`, dropped: sections 3 and 10 sentences that `root-cause.md`, `defect-root-cause.md` and `finding-propagation.md` already state, to keep the corpus cap's margin (nothing else removed).
- `fixer.md`, kept: the new sentence that the rulings bind a fixer (shortened to "bind you" to fit the per-file cap `tools/audit/briefs/fixer.md` by 4 tokens), since a fixer works under the orchestrator's briefs and the rulings; the 2026-11-15 prepr-scoping ruling in step 5.
- `proposal-triage.md`, kept: the new sentence (the round-end triage applies rulings on machinery, freeze and proposals recorded there); the card P2 machinery paragraph.
- `CLAUDE.md`, kept: the index line, now "they bind every seat, though the file is not policy"; the section "What the repository may carry" (a separate ruling of 2026-11-15 that binds every push).
- Dropped as a duplicate, by earlier rounds: any hunk making the file one of the policy files listed in `CLAUDE.md`'s policy table.

## Carries built here

- Carry 0 (card E11-N-OBJECTIVE-RECORD, part b, "Write it now (Recommended)"): `orchestrator.md` section 9 names the round's objective record under `dev/audit/yardstick/` as a closure criterion.
- Carry 1 (queue item 17, tvofi 2026-11-15): `fixer.md` step 5 states that prepr runs scoped (`PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1`, plus `PREPR_SKIP_CODE=1` for a text-only delta) and in full only where the change reaches what only it measures; `orchestrator.md` section 5 states that a fixer is a local seat only where SendMessage steering is likely, else cloud.

## Instrument changes

All kept; none reads the file's policy status. `tools/audit/seat/hooks/liveness.py` and `hooks_setup.py` (+ `instruments/hooks_setup.py.md`): the post-compaction corpus is `CLAUDE.md`, `orchestrator.md` and every `.claude/rules/` file in full, and of the instrument pages and `RULINGS.md` only what changed since the last accepted proof. They key on a file list, not on the file's classification. `sweep_template.md`: step 0 names the same read. `dev/audit/config/scopes.json` and `tests/layout.json`: classify the new tracked file (`check_scopes.py`, `layout.py` read these; the file is a record, so it is outside the policy lists).

## Mutation proof

`python3 tools/audit/seat/hooks_setup.py --self-test`: every `MUTANTS` entry this branch adds goes red against the live tree, among them `the corpus carries every page, changed or not`, `the rules are read by change`, `the rulings file is read in full`, `a changed rulings file is dropped` and `a missing core file still writes a corpus`. The diff of this round is prose only and moves no mutated line.

## Null control

In the self-test, a PostCompact with nothing changed since the proof writes the core and the rules only (`read-proof: nothing changed since the proof reads the core and the rules only (null control)`); the next case changes `RULINGS.md` and asserts it is in.

## Figures

- policy budgets: `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs --budgets` on the merge of this head onto `origin/main` `31117b1029` (a scratch merge commit, the merge-tree result): `corpus: ~69748 tokens, cap 69333 +band 500 = 69833`, `role fixer ~6252 tokens, cap 5852 +band 500 = 6352`, `role policy ~9985 tokens, cap 9958 +band 500 = 10458`; no cap changed. Paid by cutting duplicated prose in `orchestrator.md` (above), never by a raise.
- policy lint: `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs` on this head printed `TOTAL: 0 error(s) across 52 policy file(s)`; the previous head (before the fixer sentence was shortened) printed `TOTAL: 1 error(s)`, a `[budgets]` refusal of `tools/audit/briefs/fixer.md` (files_tokens).
- hook self-test: `python3 tools/audit/seat/hooks_setup.py --self-test` printed `hooks_setup self-test: 74 checks, 0 failed`.
- scopes: `python3 -I tools/audit/check_scopes.py --self-test --repo .` printed `SELF-TEST passed (every perturbed scope refused)`.
- structure: `python3 tests/structure.py` printed `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- generated rules: `node tools/policy/rules_sync.mjs --check` printed `RULES-SYNC ok`.
- prepr was run scoped, `PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1 PREPR_SKIP_CODE=1`, for this text-only delta.

## Red checks

Reds carried by earlier commits of this branch, each answered; `governance / policy-docs`, `governance / env-matrix` and `tests / fast (3.14)` are in `merge_train.py owed-reds`' set. None is red on this head by the measurements in Figures (policy lint `TOTAL: 0`; the fast job's template arm keys on that exit code).

- `governance / policy-docs`, `governance / env-matrix` and `tests / fast (3.14)`, at `91f6dc48e2`: the rulings commit replaced decisions 0010's and 0011's paths with bare numbers, which `policy_lint.mjs`'s `[citation-presence]` check refuses; repaired by citing both by path. State (b), the process existed and was not followed at that head: the figure `TOTAL: 0 error(s)` was taken before the cuts that removed the citations. Cheaper detector: `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs`, which `prepr.sh` already drives locally. No countermeasure: the detector is already in the local path.
- The same three checks at `03c8a59184`: the merged tree exceeded the corpus cap (`policy_lint.mjs --budgets`), because the branch was measured alone and main had grown. State (c), the process was followed and measured the wrong tree. Cheaper detector: `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs --budgets` on `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD`, run here and in Figures; its standing cost is one policy-lint run (about a minute). Carry: R11-INTAKE-R10-RESIDUE
- `governance / instrument-self-tests` (not in the owed set): its `check_scopes.py --self-test` refusal of `dev/programme/RULINGS.md` was repaired in `scopes.json` and `SELF-TEST passed (every perturbed scope refused)` printed on this head; its step "Refuse a self-test read set the committed table misses" is inherited from main, owned by R11-HOTFIX-MAIN-SELFTEST-RED.

## Forward-carry

- tvofi's ruling of 2026-11-15 (card "Hold delivery rows for the stamp too", in `dev/programme/RULINGS.md` under "Merges, CI and reds") has the automatic delivery-rows pull request wait and merge only with the stamp batch. The record-autofix automerge path (`tools/audit/seat/record_row.py --automerge-check`) and the board's `RECORD-OWED` line (`beat_jobs.py`, `ledger.py`, `orchestrator_tick.py`, `owed_unactioned.py`) contradict it. Control: a `record/autofix` pull request green and unmerged between stamps raises no line and is not merged; under the train's `--stamp` queue it is admitted with the stamp batch. An instrument change, held by the round-11 freeze for the round-end triage. Carry: R11-INTAKE-R10-RESIDUE

pull.title: R11-HOTFIX-MAIN-SELFTEST-RED: r11 hotfix main selftest red
pull.body:
Main red, instrument (the main-red exception to the round-11 instrument freeze). Every ci.yml push run on main on 2026-11-15 ended `failure` or `cancelled` in `governance / instrument-self-tests`, for two causes, both repaired here.

**(1) The drift step's four refusals.** `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json` missed reads main measured: the `dirs` of `dependency-graph-census` and `prepr` and the `.gitattributes` probes of `policy-lint-mutants` under `dev/audit/yardstick`, `dev/audit/yardstick/round10` and `dev/audit/rounds/round10/objective` (directories #3611 added at 646352ff), and `selftest-scope-mutants`' probe `-c`. Re-recorded the way `selftest_scope.py`'s docstring states ("Commit that file, or re-record ... and union the same way"): run 43741911544's `selftest-closures` artifact 14174287444 (main 755b7f57; zip sha256 `21243679cf94a01cb833960c4284ab52db371963081a12c6ff6f690d4b0645da`, the digest that job's log prints) unioned over main's committed table by `selftest_scope.union_record`, so `finder-overlap` and `plant-recall`, gated after that run, keep their committed entries. The diff adds exactly the ten reads the four refusals name and nothing else.

**`selftest_scope`'s own self-test does not fail.** The `FAIL` lines and the `TypeError` in job 132896968023 are the output of `selftest_scope_mutants.sh`, which prints each mutant's failing checks; that step ended "SELFTEST-SCOPE MUTANTS: every mutant refused" and passed, and the unmutated self-test step printed `selftest_scope self-test: 118 checks, 0 failed`. The `TypeError` is the "prune goes on over an unreadable table" mutant: with the `table is None` guard deleted, `prune_entries(None, ...)` raises before its `ck` line, so the mutant is killed by rc 1, not by a named check. No code defect, so no failing test was owed; the union guard of #3551 is not implicated.

**(2) The 60-minute cap on a push.** Six of main's eleven push runs on 2026-11-15 were cancelled at 60.2-60.3 minutes, the other five finished in 34.5-52.9. The variance is the runner host, not the tree: the in-line steps ran about 2.3x slower on some hosts (job 132905064799, `northcentralus`) than on others (job 132896968023, `centralus`) at near-identical heads, while the mutant step (1.0-1.4 min) and the drift fold (4.3-6.0 min) stayed flat. Every cancelled run had reached the mutant step at 57.2-59.8 minutes, which projects to about 67 minutes uncensored.

Slowest steps (min-max over the eleven runs): self-tests-outside-seat 4.9-11.6, policy-lint-mutants 2.9-7.7, the drift fold 4.3-6.0, cloud-relay 2.3-5.1, verdict-bus 1.9-4.9, ci-predictor 1.7-3.9, beat-job-rows 1.4-2.9, merge-train 1.6-2.7.

Options and the wall each buys:
- **Timeout to 90 on a push (taken).** Buys about 23 minutes over the projected slow-host worst case of about 67, i.e. about 34% headroom; costs zero seconds on a run that finishes and lengthens only a hung run, by 30 minutes. A pull request keeps 30. It does not extend the CI run's wall in practice: `codeql / Analyze (python)` in the same run takes 52.9-75.1 minutes.
- **Two shards (matrix), not taken.** Buys about half the in-line wall (a slow-host shard about 30-35 minutes including its own drift fold). Needs `scope` to filter by shard, `check` to accept a step subset rather than refuse the other shard's steps as UNMEASURED, two `selftest-closures` artifacts unioned at re-record, and a job name every reader of `instrument-self-tests` keys on to change. That is a redesign of an instrument in a freeze, not a main-red hot-fix.
- **Moving self-tests-outside-seat into the detached set, not taken.** Buys at most its 4.9-11.6 minutes and only if the runner has a free core; the slow hosts are the ones already CPU-bound, and pr_args.sh's self-test is documented in the launch step as missing its window under that contention.

**CodeQL (recommendation only, no change here).** `codeql / Analyze (python)` on main's push runs on 2026-11-15: 52.9-75.1 minutes, one cancelled at its 75-minute cap (run 43733946364, e0ad8b2b). Main's push leg scans the full tree; the pull-request leg already ignores `tests/**` and `dev/**` (codeql.yml, r10-codeql-pr-paths). Python by top directory at this head: `dev/` 1151 files, 191421 lines (863 files under `dev/audit/rounds/`, round evidence and harnesses that no product or CI path imports); `tests/` 84 files, 216677 lines (`tests/features.py` alone 92325); `tools/` 288 files, 109906 lines; `custom_components/` 92 files, 74071 lines. Recommendation: exclude `dev/audit/rounds/**` (evidence data, never executed by CI or shipped) from main's python leg; keep `tests/**`, which CI executes. This removes about 32% of the python lines (all of `dev/`) or a little less for `dev/audit/rounds/**` alone; the duration it buys is not measured here, because extraction time is dominated by `tests/features.py`, which this would keep. Measure by one `workflow_dispatch` of the leg with the exclusion before deciding.

## Head

pull.title: R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES: r10 start counter edges
pull.body:
R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES: part D of pull request #3420. Thanks to Bankaifan, who reported that the compressor start counter misses short cycles: a compressor that stops and restarts between two samples counts no start. Built on the approved design (`design/R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES` at 18655c84b6; `Design review: approve` at `design-verdict/R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES` 9900aa0068).

The counter used to sample the meter once per refresh in `_record_accuracy` and needed `START_HYSTERESIS_SAMPLES` (2) consecutive samples. It now folds the confirmed edges of `running_signal.py`, a new HA glue module. That module is the one owner of the running signal for a pump in every duty mode, duty mode off included, from the coordinator's construction (`__init__`, after the unload registration) to its release (`_release_registrations`). It owns the state listener, `wear.EdgeTracker`'s debounce, a confirm timer at `EDGE_DEBOUNCE_S`, and the subscribers: the start counter always, and the duty-switch learner while the arbiter listens. The sampled path is deleted, not kept beside it. The coordinator gains no attribute (`coordinator_multiassigned_attrs` 108 -> 107).

- **Stored counts continue.** `lifetime`, `months` and `running` keep their stored shape and `from_dict` reading, so no migration is owed. A counter is unrestored until `_async_load_ledger`'s `finally` restores it. Until then it queues edges, and the restore replays them over the stored `running`: a compressor running across the upgrade is not counted again, and an edge before the read is neither lost nor counted twice.
- **No signal counts nothing.** An unavailable, unknown or non-numeric reading is a `None` class, and the last known class holds across it. On the meter source the reader reads `None` while the immersion element runs: by the coordinator's latch, or by the reading itself being over `thermal_model.immersion_over`, now the one owner of what over means for the latch, the carve-out and the reader.
- **Premise correction (design section 4).** `_effective_cycling_cost` reads `_wear_price` (replacement cost over rated starts) and no count. The counted starts feed the wear ledger line (only at a nonzero price), the month receipt's `compressor_starts` and the insight payload. So the plan is unchanged by construction, and the count is where the null control sits.
- **Source change on an install with both a frequency sensor and a meter**: the counter now reads the frequency sensor, as part A's learner does. The retired path read the meter.
- **Release frees the coordinator.** `running_signal.detach` drops the subscribers and the reader. Both close over the coordinator, which is the weak key of the table holding them. Without that, a released coordinator was never collected (features.py's "a released coordinator is collected" read 8 referrers at the first head of this branch).
- **The refresh-held start (S7, owner ruling D1, 2026-11-15).** On the meter source a confirmed rise is not a start until `wear.HOLD_REFRESHES` (2) refreshes read the signal settled running (`wear.RiseHold`, held in front of `StartCounter.fold` by `StartCounter.hear` and `StartCounter.refresh`). A no-class edge first drops it: an element cut-in on an averaging meter reports one partial average between the on-threshold and the over level, confirmed as a rise, then over, which reads no class. A stop first passes the rise on with the stop when it rose from a stop (a run shorter than two refreshes still counts, at its own time), and drops it when it rose from no class (an element's falling average as it cuts out). The frequency source holds nothing. `running_signal.refresh` owns the per-refresh re-read and hands each subscriber's tick whether the class reads settled running, so the coordinator's refresh path is still one line. Alternatives and why each lost: the residual (owner ruling D1 refused it); the hold in the coordinator's refresh path (+3 coordinator-class lines, +1 `seam_cut_total`, a `_book_starts` call crossing into the ledger seam from `_update_current_state`: refused by `tests/structure.py`, paid by moving the tick into `running_signal`); a stop always passing the held rise on (counts the cut-out partial, killed by the S7 check); a stop always dropping it (loses every run shorter than two refreshes, the short cycles the counter exists for, killed by the blip check and the S7 control). What the hold costs: a meter start is counted up to two refresh periods late, still in the month of its first reading; a start whose rise is dropped by a meter outage inside the hold is counted again only if the meter returns reading running (a rise from no class).
- The module's import set is `wear`, `drift`, `entry_config`, `freq_control`, `inputs` and `thermal_model` (design-review carry v2). `duty_switch` imports it; it imports neither `duty_switch` nor `pump_arbiter` (pinned in features.py).

Carry 0 (owner ruling 2026-11-13, part D fired now; to round 11 if not merged when the stamp is ready): no stamp is held on this branch. origin/main was merged in twice: at 5b8f05ba4e (e8d71a241f), and at 4058469d79 (43227286fc, pull request 3532's leg rule), where `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reported conflicts in `duty_switch.py` and `tests/features.py`; see `## Head`. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 43227286fc` at 4058469d79 reports no conflict. pull.body:
`tools/pr/ci_predict.py` replayed each touched instrument-self-tests step at the head under a fixed 180 s bound and turned a timeout into rc 124; `step_replay_preds` read rc 124 at the head and 0 at the base as a predicted red, so `prepr.sh` refused clean branches on a loaded host (#3598's update and the owner-criteria opener, 2026-11-15, CI green for those steps). A timeout measures the host, not the head. Now `replay_step` returns `TIMED_OUT` (-124, never a bash rc), a head timeout is reported as the info line `UNMEASURED <step>: timed out at <s> s on this host` and is not replayed at the base or predicted. The bound is `HPO_STEP_REPLAY_TIMEOUT_S` (default 180, unparseable or non-positive falls back to 180). A real non-timeout red is predicted exactly as before. A base timeout keeps its existing path (non-zero at the base: a note left to CI).

Alternative not taken: replaying once more, base first. It doubles the cost on exactly the hosts that are slow, and a second timeout would still need this info path.

Closes: none

pull.body:
R11-PRE-ROUND-METRICS, part 1 of the group (topic r11-pre-round-metrics-p1): decision 0018 section 5's two held-out instruments, planted-defect recall and the two-finder overlap estimate, on the path to the round-11 finder start (tvofi, 2026-11-15, card E11-N-P744-SCOPE).

`tools/audit/seat/plant_recall.py` plants a held-out seat's objective bugs into the baseline export and counts recall after the judge; `tools/audit/seat/finder_overlap.py` seats a twin finder on one scopes.json seat's universe and estimates the bugs there from the judged-real overlap, reported with both seats' models. Each is self-tested in `instrument-self-tests` (steps `plant-recall`, `finder-overlap`, read sets recorded by `selftest_scope.py record`), code-owned in `.github/CODEOWNERS` (carry 0), and its run commands, before the Finders phase and after the judge, are in its `tools/audit/seat/instruments/*.py.md` page (the documented command the orchestrator runs; `audit-find.js` is not edited). The plants themselves are not written here.

Carry 0: both instruments are added to `.github/CODEOWNERS` in this pull request and built to 0018's definitions; the ones they cannot meet are the cards below. Carry 3: this part builds its two held-out instruments, recall counted after the judge (a plant lost at the verifier or the judge is a miss) with plants refused unless spread over both the natural universe and the configuration space and refused from a finder, orchestrator or evaluator planter, and the overlap reported with the two seats' models; carry 3's section-2 and section-5 reads (`product_green` over the window with `gate`'s check count, the `lead_time` clock from the roster commit, runner seconds per merge) stay with the group's later parts, as this part's brief scopes them out. Carry 1 is carry 3's text as #3575's body item 85db64f3 and is answered with carry 3; Carry 2 is carry 0's text and is answered with carry 0. Not built in this part, left to the group's later parts: Carry 4 (the `beat_jobs.py` row flagging CI re-attempts, countermeasure B of R10-RCA-SWEEP-SETTLE-LOOP), Carry 5 and Carry 6 (0018 sections 2 and 4 from the group's convergence records), Carry 7 (loop-study card L1, the loop ledger) and Carry 8 (process card P7, caused-by and found-by). Carry: R11-PRE-ROUND-METRICS

## Cards

Definitions of 0018 that cannot be met as written, returned rather than bent:

- **C1 isolated dimensions take no plant.** Section 5 plants into "the baseline export"; `audit-find.js` runs D0, D3, D9, D11, D13, D14 and D15 in `git worktree`s, where `git diff` shows every plant to the finder. `plant` refuses a tree inside a git work tree, meaning the tree itself or any ancestor of its resolved path holding a `.git` directory or file (a linked worktree's or a submodule's), so neither those worktrees nor any subdirectory of one takes a plant; a work tree with no `.git` entry on that path (its git directory named only by `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` or `core.worktree`) is outside the guard, and `audit-find.js`'s `git worktree add` writes the `.git` file it reads. Recall is read over the export's dimensions only and the seven isolated ones have no recall. Owner choice: accept that, or plant those worktrees as a commit the wall hides (not built).
- **C2 when a finding "finds" a plant.** 0018 defines recall as found / planted and names no matching rule. Built: a judged finding names a plant when its `files` hold the plant's file and the plant's `symbol` is a whole word of its `instrumented_symbol`, `title` or `claim`; every match is printed with the finding ids so the rule can be audited per plant.
- **C3 the overlap is counted after the judge.** Section 5 says "finding n1 and n2 with m shared" without a stage. Built as recall is (section 4 item 3): a seat's finding counts when its canonical finding is judged `verified` or `weakened`, and m is the bugs the judge's dedup merged across the two seats.
- **C4 the models are declared, not recorded.** No round record holds a seat's model (`finding.schema`, `JUDGE.json`, `reports-<box>.json`); the pair record carries the models the orchestrator dispatches with, which nothing re-reads.

## Head

`54a0f39d135bfdf176ac0ab0323d92eb2925a454` merges the authored code head `686f63afa1e74e5cfca97cfb0d7b1442fc1948a9`.

686f63afa1e74e5cfca97cfb0d7b1442fc1948a9, measured at origin/main 646352ff1364bcbc25875b949072f98e7a53b5fe, 2026-11-15T15:11:31Z.

## Review round 1

Answers `Fix review: blocked 56a8a61b92480e770943483d37f08306ae4ee694 class-open` (probe/rev-3612-86286f2c), from ebd654c3.

- **Block: the `.git` guard read only the tree's root.** `refusals()` now walks the tree's resolved path and every parent and refuses at the first holding `.git`, a directory or a file. Chosen over `git -C <tree> rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`: both refuse a linked worktree (the walk tests `.exists()`, so a `.git` file counts; the `git file` mutant, `.is_dir()`, is killed by the linked-worktree case), but `rev-parse` fails open, planting whenever it exits non-zero for a reason other than being outside a work tree (no `git` binary on the path, `safe.directory` refusing a repository owned by another user), while the walk needs no binary and refuses on any `.git` entry. What the walk does not see is in C1. The self-test uses `git rev-parse` as the oracle: each refused tree is first confirmed inside a work tree by git, and the null-control directory confirmed outside.
- **Finding: two plants in one file.** `plant()` no longer runs a bounded replace per plant against the running text; plants sharing a file are spliced at their old text's place in the original file, last place first, and `refusals()` refuses two plants whose old texts overlap. A plant whose `new` text holds another plant's `old` text is now planted correctly rather than refused (case `two plants in one file each land at the original place of their old text`, pinned by the `splice order` mutant). The unbounded-replace survivor the review named no longer has a site: no `.replace` is left in `plant()`.

## Mutation proof

Each self-test edits a copy of its own production code above its self-test marker, one mutant per predicate, and fails unless the named case fails: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/plant_recall.py --self-test` prints `mutant killed` for 27 predicates (planter ban and its normalisation, unnamed planter, a plant in neither space (`space known`), a plant whose file is absent (`missing file`), the merged verdict spelled with the `into` field (`merged field`), `.git` tree, `.git` in an ancestor (`git ancestors`: the walk cut to the tree alone), `.git` as a file (`git file`), list inside the tree, overlapping old texts (`overlap`), splice order (`splice order`: ascending instead of last place first), both spaces, config cell, old text once, a plant changing nothing, empty list, the real verdicts and weakened among them, the file and the whole-word arms of a finding naming a plant, LOST against MISSED, the merge chain and its text spelling, and the three unread guards); `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/finder_overlap.py --self-test` for 12 (seat in scopes, both models, the box key, shared, the estimator, unseen, one model, the three unread guards, the twin's id range (`twin ids`), `--round` required (`round required`); the verdict and merge rules it reads are `plant_recall.resolve`'s, the one reader of the judge's merge grammar, mutated in that file's run). Run alone, the `old once` mutant (`if n != 1:` to `if n < 1:`) turns `FAIL plant: an old text twice in the file is refused`.

Diff mutants (`fixer.md` step 2): `MUTANT_CMD="python3 -I tools/audit/seat/finder_overlap.py --self-test --no-mutants" MUTANT_IN_PLACE=1 bash tools/pr/prepr.sh <body>`; prepr's draw of the diff's first 40 mutants falls wholly in `finder_overlap.py`. Before this round's last commit it printed five `SURVIVED`; two were killable and are killed by the two new `finder_overlap.py` cases above (`--round` default 0 to 1, `TWIN_FROM` 71 to 72). The rest are equivalent: `finder_overlap.py:43 CONST_SWAP` (`sys.path.insert(1, ...)`: the script's own directory is the only place `plant_recall` is found, at either position), `finder_overlap.py:102 RETURN_DEL` (`load()`'s `except` arm returning `None` explicitly, which falling off the end also returns), `finder_overlap.py:108 CONST_SWAP` (`__doc__.split("\n", 2)[0]`, the same first line as a split at 1). The draw still prints `finder_overlap.py:46 CONST_SWAP TWIN_FROM = 72` as `SURVIVED`, a false survivor: run alone through `mutant_run.py --spec` (old text `\nTWIN_FROM = 71\n`) it prints `KILLED twin ids`, and the equivalent `sys.path.insert(1, ...)` run alone prints `SURVIVED path pos`, while the two in one spec print `KILLED` for both (see `## Forward-carry`).

Failing first: the head's `cases()` driven over ebd654c3's module (a scratch driver loads `git show ebd654c3:tools/audit/seat/plant_recall.py` as the production module and the head's file for `cases(prod, tests)`) fails five cases: `a tree holding .git is refused`, `a subdirectory of a git work tree is refused`, `a linked worktree (its .git a file) and a subdirectory of one are refused`, `two plants in one file each land at the original place of their old text`, `two plants whose old texts overlap in one file are refused`. The first fails there on the refusal's new text, which those cases match; ebd654c3 did refuse a `.git` at the tree's own root. The same driver over the head's own module fails none.

## Null control

Each instrument's null control is an empty input printing `unread (<why>)` and no digit: `plant_recall.py recall` over an empty directory prints `recall  unread (no plant list, or an empty one)`, and `finder_overlap.py estimate` over one prints `overlap unread (no pair record)`; both are self-test cases with a mutant each. A sound plant list over both spaces is refused nothing; a plain directory outside any work tree, which `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` confirms is outside one, is refused nothing and planted; two plants with disjoint old texts in one file are refused nothing; and a scopes seat with two models is seated (self-test cases).

## Figures

- Self-tests, at the head: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/plant_recall.py --self-test` ends `plant_recall self-test: ok (with mutants)`; `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/finder_overlap.py --self-test` ends `finder_overlap self-test: ok (with mutants)`.
- End to end on real data, illustrative plants (not round-11 plants): a two-plant list (P01 natural in `currency.py:money_scale`, P02 config cell `price_shape=flat` in `optimizer.py:_multi_start_minimize`) planted into a `git archive HEAD custom_components` copy by `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/plant_recall.py plant --plants <list> --tree <copy> --population <check_scopes.py --population output> --not orchestrator --not evaluator` prints two `PLANTED` lines; a second run refuses both (old text 0 times); `--not Demo_Planter` against planter `demo-planter` refuses. `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/plant_recall.py recall --plants <list> --judge-input dev/audit/rounds/round10/JUDGE-INPUT.json --judge dev/audit/rounds/round10/JUDGE.json` prints recall 1/2: P02 FOUND by D0-s1-01 and D0-s2-01 (judged weakened and verified), P01 MISSED. - `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/finder_overlap.py estimate` over round 10's D0-s1 (`reports-B1.json`) and D0-s2 (`reports-B2.json`) as a stand-in pair (two universes, so an illustration of the count, not an estimate) and `dev/audit/rounds/round10/JUDGE.json` prints n1=1 n2=1 m=0, estimate 3.0, 1.0 unseen; checked by hand from the two reports' ids and their verdicts (D0-s1-01 weakened, D0-s2-01 verified, no merge between them): (1+1)(1+1)/(0+1) - 1 = 3. The same with the twin's report absent prints `overlap unread (a seat's report is missing ...)`; `seat --seat D0-s9` refuses (no such seat).
- The review's subdirectory reproduction at both ends, rested on a scratch driver in the shape of the review's ev/git-subdir-gap.txt, not in the tree: a fresh repository holding a committed module in a subdirectory, a linked worktree of it, and a plain copy outside any work tree, each given a two-plant list over both spaces by `plant`, then a diff stat taken in both work trees. At ebd654c3 the repository's subdirectory and the linked worktree's subdirectory each print two `PLANTED` lines with rc=0, and each work tree's diff stat shows the planted module changed. At the head both print `plant: REFUSED <tree> is inside the git work tree at <its work tree>: a plant there shows in git diff` with rc=1, and both diff stats are empty. Control, at both ends: the plain copy prints two `PLANTED` lines with rc=0 and holds both plants. The in-tree reproduction of the same property is the self-test's three work-tree cases and its null control, each tree first classified by `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`.
- Class enumeration (`fixer.md` step 8): the class is a guard that decides whether a planted tree is visible to a finder through git. Rule: `git grep -nE "[\"']\.git[\"']" -- tools/audit/seat/ tools/audit/*.py`. It returns `plant_recall.py`'s guard, closed in this diff, and its own self-test lines; every other hit (`fold_ledger.py`, `machinery_ratchet.py`, `merge_throughput.py`, `beatd.py`, `flow_metrics.py`, `review_strength.py`, `roster_edit.py`, `roster_lib.py`, `roster_queue.py`) is a fixture path or a directory filter inside a test repository, not a guard on a planted tree. `finder_overlap.py` writes only its pair record (`--out`) and plants nothing.
- The self-test's git repositories are built by `tests/throwaway_git.py`'s `throwaway_git_init` (prepr's throwaway-git step refused a raw `git init` in the first cut); its mutant copies, run from a temporary directory, take the tests directory as `--tests`. `python3 -I tests/throwaway_git.py --check` prints `0 raw git init or clone site(s) refused`. `plant-recall`'s read set in `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json` is re-recorded by `python3 -I tools/ci/selftest_scope.py record --step plant-recall` and now holds `tests/throwaway_git.py`.
- Gate scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)` prints `MODE: FULL` (`tools/ci/selftest_closures.json` is a gate file), left to CI; `python3 -I tools/ci/selftest_scope.py select --base origin/main` prints `MODE: FULL` (`governance.yml` changed). `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
